Section 10.2 Linearity and Accuracy

線性與準確度
PDA Technical Report No. 33 (Revised 2026) | p131-p144

本章學習目標

  • 理解為何「線性 Linearity」在微生物學方法驗證中的意義不同於分析化學方法——它是用來把 Section 10.1 在特定濃度點得到的準確度（accuracy）結論，延伸到未測試濃度範圍的橋樑，而非單點校正的必要條件
  • 掌握加權線性迴歸（Weighted Linear Regression, WLR）與 Poisson 迴歸兩種對計數（counts）建立濃度反應曲線（concentration-response curve）的方法，理解兩者對變異數異質性（heteroscedasticity）的不同處理方式，以及如何用截距、斜率、R² 與二次項檢定判斷線性/比例性（proportionality）
  • 理解 Mitscherlich 函數如何將非線性濃度反應關係一般化，並能辨識何時簡化為 log-linear、linear 或 proportional 模型；比較非線性 Poisson 迴歸與加權非線性迴歸兩種配適方法（以 AICC 判斷優劣）
  • 能夠說明「以模型為本（model-based）」的濃度反應曲線比較法，相較於逐濃度（per-concentration）分類變數比較法，如何能以更少的樣本數把非劣性（non-inferiority）結論延伸到更廣的濃度範圍，並理解其在 CDMO 方法驗證與放行策略上的實務效益
10.2 Linearity and Accuracy 線性與準確度

原文內容 Original Text

For analytical measurement systems, linearity is an important validation parameter, because the analytical measurement system makes use of a reference sample in routine analysis to determine the concentration value of an unknown sample. The reference and unknown sample are being tested in one analytical run and, for each run, a run-specific single-point calibration line is created that goes through the origin and through the response of the reference sample (the green line and dot in Figure 10.2-1). Since the true concentration value of the reference sample is known (xR), the observed concentration value of the unknown sample is obtained by the concentration of the calibration line (xU) that matches the value of the line to the response of the unknown sample (the red arrows and dot in Figure 10.2-1). To be able to use such a procedure in routine analysis for analytical measurement systems, it is imperative that the concentration-response curve is linear and goes through the origin. Thus, for single-point calibration models for analytical measurement systems what is needed is proportionality.

Figure 10.2-1 Visualization of the Estimated Concentration for an Unknown Sample Using a Linear Calibration Line for the Reference Sample in Analytical Measurement Systems

In microbiology, linearity has a different purpose, and should support the validation parameter accuracy as conducted in Section 10.1. If accuracy is achieved at each concentration level that has been tested in an accuracy experiment (Sections 10.1.1, 10.1.2, and 10.1.3), that accuracy only applies for the tested concentration levels and cannot automatically be guaranteed (and may fail) at non-tested concentration levels within the full interval. In order to extend the accuracy at specific concentration levels to all non-tested concentration levels within the spiked interval, a linear or, more precisely, a monotonic concentration-recovery curve is required. This operation is a smooth concentration curve that is nondecreasing or nonincreasing over the interval of interest where the recovery is defined as the mean count of the AMM/RMM divided by the true concentration level (often the spiked concentration level or a precise estimate of the concentration level with the CMM) at which the mean count is observed. A linear or monotonic concentration-recovery curve guarantees that the worst bias or lack of accuracy is attained at the two outer concentration levels in the experiment (the green dots and green line in Figure 10.2-2). The ideal recovery for the AMM/RMM is 100%, or more if non-CFU signals are generated in the AMM/RMM. Therefore, the worst accuracy for the green recovery results in Figure 10.2-2 occurs at the last (or sixth) spiked concentration, as it is the lowest recovery across the range of concentration levels in the interval of the experiment (the green dots and green line in Figure 10.2-2).

Figure 10.2-2 Visualization of Results from a Linear Concentration Response Curve (Green) and Results from a Non-linear Concentration Response Curve (Blue) Expressed in the Spiked Concentration and its Consequence for Accuracy

The blue dots in Figure 10.2-2, on the other hand, show that accuracy may potentially hold for each spiked concentration level in the experiment separately. In this case, the blue dots (the mean recoveries) are all away from the non-inferiority margin of 70%, even though some results are still close to this boundary. Following the expected recovery of the blue nonlinear concentration-recovery curve in Figure 10.2-2, however, the accuracy would most likely fail at specific untested concentration levels between the fourth and fifth spiked concentration levels. Indeed, the expected recovery reaches below the non-inferiority margin of 70%. Thus, without linearity or monotonicity of the concentration-recovery curve, there is no guarantee that accuracy holds across the full range of spiked concentration levels even if it has been demonstrated that non-inferiority holds at all the spiked concentration levels in the accuracy experiment.

To determine linearity for the concentration-recovery curve, the following mathematical formula is used:

E(y|λ) / λ  =  β0 + β1λ

Where: E(y|λ) = expected concentration of the AMM/RMM of an arbitrary test sample that is tested at the true concentration level λ; λ = true concentration level; E(y|λ)/λ would represent the recovery (not expressed in percentages); β0 = intercept of the linear concentration-recovery curve; β1 = slope of the linear concentration-recovery curve.

The expected concentration E(y|λ) would be estimated with the mean counts at the spiked concentration level observed in the experiment, and the true concentration level would either be estimated by a precise estimate from the CMM* or taken by the spiked concentration level. If a stricter assumption is made and it is assumed that the slope β1 is equal to zero (0), the concentration-recovery curve becomes a horizontal line, and the intercept represents the expected recovery for all concentration levels. This was demonstrated in Section 10.1.3 when the recovery of the AMM/RMM against the CMM was constant. Under this stricter assumption, the concentration-response curve for the AMM/RMM is then proportional to the true concentration level λ, that is, E(y|λ) = β0λ as was discussed regarding the single-point calibration model of an analytical measurement system. Thus, if proportionality can be shown for the concentration-response curve, this demonstrates a more defined linearity needed to support that accuracy has been demonstrated across the full interval of spike levels.

*Note: In many linearity experiments, the number of replicates taken at each concentration for the CMM is often too small to be able to obtain a precise estimate of the true concentration (too much variability), and a regression analysis where the mean counts of the CMM are used as independent variables and the mean counts of the AMM/RMM are considered the dependent variable may lead to incorrect estimates of the intercept and slope of the regression line.

In microbiology, however, it is common to demonstrate a linear concentration-response curve, that is, E(y|λ) = α + β0λ, where the mean counts of the AMM/RMM are modeled as a function of the true concentration. Unfortunately, this concentration-response curve does not lead to a linear concentration-recovery curve, since the concentration-recovery curve becomes E(y|λ)/λ = β0 + α/λ which is no longer a linear function of the true concentration λ. Demonstrating a linear concentration-response curve is still appropriate, however, because the concentration-recovery function remains monotonic (i.e., it is a non-increasing function when α is positive), which is necessary for the concentration-recovery curve to support the validation parameter accuracy. Additionally, demonstrating a log-linear concentration-response curve (i.e., log(E(y|λ)) = α + β0log(λ) with log the natural logarithm) also leads to a monotonic concentration-recovery curve: E(y|λ)/λ = exp{α} · λβ0−1.

Thus, when it can be shown that the concentration response curve is linear or even log-linear, there is no need to evaluate the concentration-recovery curve due to the explanation given here. However, when other forms of concentration response curves, which are discussed in the text above, are identified, the concentration-recovery curve may need to be studied directly to be able to support the validation parameter accuracy (see Section 10.2.3).

Using the data from Table 10.1-1 to illustrate the evaluation of concentration-response and concentration-recovery curves, visualizing the mean counts against the spiked concentration levels in Figure 10.2-3A and Figure 10.2-3B will help evaluate the possible choices in curves. The mean counts have been linearly connected without building a regression equation at this point. Qualitatively, the concentration-response curves (top two figures) show what would likely be a linear function of the spiked concentration level, but the concentration-recovery curves may deviate from linearity, mostly because the results at the lowest concentration level seem to be somewhat higher than what can be expected from linearity of the other concentrations. However, the variation in the replicated recoveries at the lowest concentration level is also relatively large, which makes this determination difficult. Finally, it can also be seen that the variability in the replicated counts is nonconstant across the spiked concentrations levels (heteroscedasticity), and this should be addressed when an appropriate regression equation is being constructed from the observed data.

Figure 10.2-3A Visualization of the Mean Counts with Respect to the Spiked Concentration Levels

Figure 10.2-3B Visualization of the Mean Counts with Respect to the Spiked Concentration Levels

導師解析 Tutorial Commentary

核心概念解析 Key Concepts

Linearity（線性，此處指濃度反應/濃度回收曲線的線性或單調性): 在分析化學儀器（如 HPLC）裡，線性是「單點校正」能否成立的先決條件——沒有線性就無法用一個參考品的訊號去回推未知樣品的濃度。但在微生物學方法（AMM/RMM）裡，線性扮演的角色完全不同：它是把 Section 10.1 在少數幾個 spiked concentration（如 5、25、50、100、150、250 CFU）上已證明的準確度（accuracy），「安全地延伸」到這些濃度之間、實驗中沒有實際測試過的濃度值的橋樑。

Monotonic concentration-recovery curve（單調濃度回收曲線): Recovery 定義為「平均計數 ÷ 真實濃度」。曲線只要是單調不增或不減（不一定要是直線），就能保證：只要曲線兩端（最低與最高濃度）的回收率都通過非劣性瑪margin，中間所有未測試濃度的回收率也一定落在兩端之間——這就是 Figure 10.2-2 中綠色曲線（線性）為何比藍色曲線（非線性、U 形）更值得信賴的原因：藍色曲線在中段會「凹」到 70% 門檻以下，即使兩端和多數測試點都合格。

比喻說明 Analogy

把準確度實驗想像成「量體溫的溫度計只在 3 個刻度上做過校正（36°C、38°C、40°C），而且每個刻度都準」。如果溫度計的誤差曲線是「單調」的（誤差隨溫度穩定變化，沒有忽大忽小），你可以放心推論 37°C、39°C 也準確。但如果溫度計的誤差曲線像雲霄飛車一樣忽高忽低（非單調），即使 3 個校正點都準，中間的 37°C 完全有可能誤差爆表——這正是 Figure 10.2-2 藍色曲線在第四、五個濃度點之間掉到 70% 門檻以下的情境：兩端測試點合格，不代表中間安全。

重點提示 Key Notes

原文特別提醒：若能證明濃度反應曲線是 linear（E(y|λ)=α+β0λ）或 log-linear（log(E(y|λ))=α+β0log(λ)），則濃度回收曲線「自動」保持單調，不需要另外再去驗證回收曲線本身——因為線性/log-linear 濃度反應曲線在數學上必然導出單調的回收函數。但要小心：linear concentration-response curve（E(y|λ)=α+β0λ, α≠0）並不等於 linear concentration-recovery curve；回收曲線會變成 E(y|λ)/λ=β0+α/λ，這是一條非線性但單調的曲線。這個區分正是 Section 10.2.1 與 10.2.2 為什麼要分別對「計數」本身建模，而不是直接對「回收率」建模的原因。

公式與計算 Formula

濃度回收曲線（Concentration-Recovery Curve）:

E(y|λ) / λ = β0 + β1·λ

E(y|λ) = 在真實濃度 λ 下，AMM/RMM 任一測試樣品的期望計數
λ      = 真實濃度水準（spiked concentration）
E(y|λ)/λ = 回收率（recovery，未乘以 100%）
β0     = 濃度回收曲線的截距
β1     = 濃度回收曲線的斜率（若 β1=0，回收曲線為水平線 = 比例性 proportionality 成立）

Log-linear 濃度反應曲線導出的回收曲線:

log(E(y|λ)) = α + β0·log(λ)
        ⇒  E(y|λ)/λ = exp{α} · λ^(β0 − 1)   （對 λ 單調）

圖表解讀 Figure Analysis

Figure 10.2-1 呈現的是分析化學儀器的單點校正邏輯：以已知濃度 xR 的參考品訊號 yR 建立通過原點的校正線，再用未知樣品訊號 yU 反推其濃度 xU。這個邏輯的前提是曲線「必須」通過原點且為直線——這正是本節開頭用來對比微生物學方法的參照系統。

Figure 10.2-2 是本節最關鍵的教學圖：綠色（線性/單調）與藍色（非線性、U 形）兩條回收曲線都在多數測試點合格，但藍色曲線在中段（第 4～5 個濃度點之間）跌破 70% 非劣性門檻，證明「逐點合格」不能保證「連續濃度範圍內都合格」，這正是線性驗證存在的意義。

Figure 10.2-3A/3B 用 Table 10.1-1 的實際資料呈現：3A 為濃度反應（計數 vs. 濃度，兩方法皆呈現近似直線但有異質變異），3B 則是回收率（%）vs. 濃度，可觀察到最低濃度點（5 CFU）的回收率偏高且變異很大，這也是後續 10.2.1／10.2.2 節要用迴歸模型正式檢定線性、而非僅憑肉眼判讀圖形的原因。

實務應用 Practical Application

對 CDMO 而言，客戶送驗的 AMM/RMM 通常只在 3～6 個 spiked concentration 做過驗證實驗，但放行測試時樣品的實際微生物濃度幾乎不可能剛好落在這幾個驗證點上。若方法驗證報告只呈現「各濃度點都合格」而未證明線性或單調性，等於留下一個法規與科學上的缺口：無法保證兩個驗證點之間的濃度也準確。因此在審查客戶或內部 AMM/RMM 驗證報告時，應主動要求提供 Section 10.2.1／10.2.2 的迴歸分析結果，而不只是 Section 10.1 的逐濃度回收率表。

練習思考 Practice Questions

  1. 如果某 AMM/RMM 的濃度反應曲線被證明是 log-linear（log(E(y|λ))=α+β0·log(λ)），為什麼可以不用另外再檢驗濃度回收曲線的單調性？
  2. Figure 10.2-2 中藍色曲線在多數測試點都通過 70% 門檻，為什麼仍然不能宣稱該方法在整個濃度區間都符合非劣性？
10.2.1 Weighted Linear Regression Analysis on the Counts 對計數進行加權線性迴歸分析

原文內容 Original Text

To create a concentration-response curve, it must first be assumed that the counts can be approximately modelled by the following linear regression equation:

y  =  α + βλ + ε

Where: y = a count that is observed at spiked concentration level λ; α = intercept of the line; β = slope of the regression line; λ = spiked concentration level; ε = residual having a normal distribution with mean zero and variance σ²(λ).

Here, it is assumed that the variance in the replicated counts at spiked concentration level λ also depends on the spiked concentration (as seen from the data). If the residual variance varies with the concentration, the regression analysis should weight the observed value with the inverse variance. This type of analyses is programmed in any general-purpose software package.

Table 10.2.1-1 shows the estimates of the intercept and slope with a 95% confidence interval, if this weighted linear regression analysis is applied to the counts of the AMM/RMM and CMM separately.

Based on the estimated results, it follows that the intercept of the regression line for the AMM/RMM is not statistically different from zero (0) (the 95% confidence interval contains the value zero (0)). If linearity is satisfied for the AMM/RMM, that is, no better relations describe the data, the AMM/RMM satisfies proportionality, implying a constant concentration-recovery curve with a recovery close to 77.8% (i.e., the slope multiplied with 100, for every concentration (see Section 10.2 and Section 10.2.2). On the other hand, the 95% confidence interval for the intercept of the CMM positively indicates that the intercept deviates from zero (since the number zero (0) is not contained in the 95% confidence interval), implying that the CMM has a nonzero background enumeration level of 1.922 CFUs for blank samples if linearity holds true. In other words, based on the estimated intercept, the CMM would generate false positives when test samples do not contain microorganisms.

To investigate the linearity, the explained variation (R²) with the fitted regression line is equal to 98.4 for the AMM/RMM and 99.6 for the CMM. These values can be obtained from the output of general-purpose software packages when the weighted linear regression analyses are performed. These high values for the R² are often considered as evidence for satisfying linearity, since there seems hardly any variation left that could be explained by possible nonlinearity. While there is some truth in this, a high R² can also be achieved when a wide range of concentrations is used and linearity is violated. A more formal way of investigating linearity is to test for a deviation from linearity, where a quadratic term for concentration level is included by using the regression equation y = α + βλ + γλ² + ε, and then testing whether the coefficient γ is equal to zero. When this extended regression model is applied, the p-values of 0.821 and 0.189 for the AMM/RMM and CMM, respectively, can be obtained, indicating that there is no evidence for nonlinearity for both microbiological methods. Thus, the conclusion is that both microbiological methods satisfy linearity.

The conclusion of linearity for the AMM/RMM with the attained non-inferiority of accuracy for concentration levels 50, 100, 150, and 250 CFU with the normal distribution in Table 10.1.1-1 implies that non-inferiority is attained for any concentration level between 50 and 250 CFU.

導師解析 Tutorial Commentary

核心概念解析 Key Concepts

Weighted Linear Regression（WLR，加權線性迴歸): 標準線性迴歸假設每個資料點的殘差變異數相同（同質變異，homoscedastic）。但微生物計數資料存在異質變異（heteroscedasticity）——濃度越高，計數的變異數通常也越大（可回想 Table 10.1-1 的 variance 欄：5 CFU 時 variance≈4.7，250 CFU 時 variance≈388）。WLR 用「反變異數」作為權重，讓變異小（較可信）的濃度點在迴歸配適時佔更大話語權，避免高濃度的大變異「拖垮」整條迴歸線的精確度。

Proportionality via Intercept Test（用截距檢定比例性): 截距 α 的 95% CI 是否包含 0，是判斷「是否存在系統性背景訊號（假陽性）」的關鍵：AMM/RMM 的 95% CI (-0.975, 2.634) 包含 0 → 沒有證據顯示背景訊號 → 支持比例性；CMM 的 95% CI (0.721, 3.122) 不包含 0 → 統計上顯著非零 → 暗示 CMM 本身就有約 1.922 CFU 的背景計數（可能來自試劑或培養基本身的微生物負荷）。

比喻說明 Analogy

加權迴歸就像做民意調查時「依樣本可信度分配權重」：一份訪問了 10,000 人、抽樣誤差很小的調查，理應比一份只訪問 30 人、誤差很大的調查更有話語權。同理，WLR 讓變異小的濃度點（通常是低濃度）主導迴歸線的精確度，而不是被高濃度的大波動牽著走。至於截距是否為零，可以想像成檢查一台體重計「沒有人站上去時，指針是否歸零」——CMM 的截距顯著不為零，就像體重計空秤時仍顯示 1.9 公斤，代表儀器本身有系統性偏移。

重點提示 Key Notes

原文特別提醒：高 R² 不等於線性成立。R²=98.4%（AMM/RMM）、99.6%（CMM）看似非常漂亮，但當濃度範圍拉得很寬（本例橫跨 5～250 CFU，達 50 倍），即使真實關係是非線性的，R² 仍可能因為整體趨勢一致而顯得很高。因此原文採用更嚴謹的二次項顯著性檢定（在模型中加入 γλ² 並檢定 γ=0）作為線性的正式證據，而非僅憑 R² 判讀——這是撰寫或審查方法驗證報告時容易忽略、但法規查廠時常被提問的重點。

公式與計算 Formula

加權線性迴歸模型：
y = α + β·λ + ε,   ε ~ N(0, σ²(λ))

y  = 在濃度 λ 下觀察到的計數
α  = 迴歸線截距（濃度為 0 時的期望計數 → 背景/假陽性訊號）
β  = 迴歸線斜率（× 100 = 回收率 %，若截距=0）
λ  = spiked concentration
σ²(λ) = 隨濃度而變的殘差變異數 → 以反變異數加權

線性正式檢定（二次項法）：
y = α + β·λ + γ·λ² + ε
H0: γ = 0  (線性成立)
AMM/RMM: p = 0.821 → 不拒絕 H0 → 線性成立
CMM:      p = 0.189 → 不拒絕 H0 → 線性成立

實務應用 Practical Application

當一套 CMM（例如平板計數法）被發現截距顯著不為零，代表該方法本身在「零濃度」的參考基準上就存在偏移。對 CDMO 而言，這個訊息在跨方法比對（AMM/RMM vs. CMM）時極為關鍵：如果只單純比較兩方法的回收率而不校正 CMM 本身的系統性偏移，可能會錯誤高估或低估 AMM/RMM 的真實準確度。這也是為什麼 Section 10.1.2 特別針對 CMM 本身也做了對 spiked concentration 的準確度分析。

練習思考 Practice Questions

  1. 為什麼不能只看 R² 值高（如 98.4%）就直接宣稱濃度反應曲線是線性的？應該補做哪一個統計檢定？
  2. 若 CMM 的截距 95% CI 不包含 0，這對後續用 CMM 作為「真實濃度」估計值（如 Section 10.2 開頭腳註所提）會有什麼影響？

10.2.2 Poisson Regression Analysis on the Counts 對計數進行 Poisson 迴歸分析

原文內容 Original Text

An alternative analysis on the count data that would also deal with the heteroscedasticity is Poisson regression. Instead of assuming normality for the counts, the counts are assumed to be Poisson-distributed. Furthermore, Poisson regression typically uses a logarithmic link function, which would guarantee that the intercept can never become negative. This is different in a weighted linear regression analysis, where the intercept can become negative. Additionally, Poisson regression does not require weights, since the Poisson-distribution dictates that the variance in the replicates equal the mean of the replicates. (Poisson regression analysis is available in many general-purpose statistical software packages.)

In Poisson regression (with the default log-link function), the concentration-response curve is assumed to take the following form:

E(y|λ)  =  exp{ α + β · ψ(λ) }

Where: E(y|λ) = expected concentration of the AMM/RMM of an arbitrary test sample that is tested at the true concentration level λ; λ = spiked concentration level; ψ(λ) = transformed concentration level; α = intercept; β = slope.

For validation of microbiological methods, the two typical transformations are the logarithmic transformation (ψ(λ) = log(λ)) and no transformation (i.e., the identity function ψ(λ) = λ). For the logarithmic transformation, the concentration-response curve is forced through the origin (when the slope β > 0), implying no false-positive rate or background noise. Moreover, when the slope is close to one (β ≈ 1), the value 100% · exp{α} represents the recovery of the microbiological method with respect to all spiked concentration levels. When the slope is larger than one (β > 1), the microbiological method has difficulty in enumerating microorganisms at a lower concentration, but it improves the enumeration when concentrations are getting higher. When the slope is less than one (β < 1), the microbiological method has more difficulty in enumerating microorganism at higher concentration, often due to saturation problems. If the identity function is taken, the value exp{α} represents the mean count or background noise at blank samples, which is always positive, although this does not guarantee a more sensitive enumeration at the lower concentration.

Fitting the Poisson regression model to the data of Table 10.1-1 for both microbiological methods separately, using the logarithm of the concentration level (i.e., ψ(λ) = log(λ)), leads to the estimates of the parameters and their 95% confidence intervals shown in Table 10.2.2-1.

Both microbiological methods show a slope that is less than one, indicating some saturation at higher concentration levels. The CMM has a slope that deviates from one, since one is not contained in the 95% confidence interval. However, the slope for AMM/RMM cannot be demonstrated to be different from one, since the value one is contained in the 95% confidence interval, indicating that the AMM/RMM may satisfy proportionality. Assuming the assumption of proportionality holds, the recovery of the AMM/RMM against the spiked concentration levels is approximately equal to 90.5% (= 100 · exp (−0.0999)) for all concentration levels within 5 to 250 CFUs, although a better estimate is obtained when the slope is fixed to the value one in the Poisson regression analysis.

導師解析 Tutorial Commentary

核心概念解析 Key Concepts

Poisson Regression（Poisson 迴歸): 不假設常態分布，而是直接假設計數服從 Poisson 分布——這在生物學上更貼近真實：微生物在懸浮液中隨機均勻分布時，取樣得到的計數本質上就是 Poisson 隨機變數。Poisson 分布有一個特性「均值=變異數」，因此模型「自動」處理了異質變異問題，不需要像 WLR 那樣額外估計權重。

Log-link Function 與斜率 β 的三種情境: 使用對數連結函數 log(E(y|λ))=α+β·ψ(λ) 時：β≈1 代表比例性成立（回收率=100%·exp{α}，對所有濃度皆適用）；β>1 代表低濃度偵測較弱、高濃度轉強（常見於訊號需要「累積」才被偵測到的技術）；β<1 代表高濃度出現飽和效應（訊號在高濃度時不再線性成長，常見於光學/螢光類方法的偵測器飽和）。

比喻說明 Analogy

可以把 β>1 想像成「新手司機」：起步（低濃度）時反應遲鈍、容易漏抓訊號，但速度（濃度）拉高後抓得越來越準；β<1 則像「相機在強光下過曝」：光線（濃度）越強，感光元件（偵測器）越容易飽和，多出來的濃度已經無法再被完整記錄成比例增加的訊號——這正是高濃度計數常見的「封頂」現象。

重點提示 Key Notes

WLR（10.2.1）與 Poisson 迴歸（10.2.2）用同一組資料（Table 10.1-1）卻得到「不同角度」的線性結論：WLR 判斷 AMM/RMM「截距不顯著異於 0」支持比例性；Poisson 迴歸判斷 AMM/RMM「斜率 β 的 95% CI 包含 1」也支持比例性——兩者殊途同歸，但檢定的參數與模型假設完全不同（常態 vs. Poisson、線性尺度 vs. 對數尺度）。實務上建議兩種方法都執行，並在 10.1.1.3 節「Lack-of-Fit Analyses」（overdispersion 檢定、AICC 比較）輔助判斷哪一種分布假設更貼近實際資料，而非任選一種。

公式與計算 Formula

Poisson 迴歸濃度反應曲線（log-link）：
E(y|λ) = exp{ α + β·ψ(λ) }

ψ(λ) = log(λ)  → 曲線強制通過原點（無背景訊號），
                 β≈1 時回收率 = 100%·exp{α}
ψ(λ) = λ       → exp{α} = 空白樣品的期望計數（背景訊號）

AMM/RMM（假設比例性成立）：
回收率 ≈ 100 × exp(−0.0999) = 90.5%   (5–250 CFU 全區間適用)

實務應用 Practical Application

若某 AMM/RMM 平台的 Poisson 迴歸結果顯示斜率 β 顯著小於 1（高濃度飽和），CDMO 在導入該技術做「早期汙染監測」時應特別留意：高濃度污染事件（大量微生物入侵）反而可能因偵測器飽和而被低估其嚴重程度。這類技術限制應納入方法適用範圍（method scope）與偏差調查 SOP 的判讀邏輯中，避免高濃度異常事件被系統性低估。

練習思考 Practice Questions

  1. 若 Poisson 迴歸估得某方法斜率 β 的 95% CI 為 (1.05, 1.42)，這代表該方法在低濃度與高濃度的偵測能力分別呈現什麼型態？
  2. 為什麼 Poisson 迴歸「不需要」像加權線性迴歸那樣額外指定權重來處理異質變異？

10.2.3 Comparability on Accuracy of Alternative/Rapid Microbiological Methods Against Conventional Methods Using Concentration-Response Curves 以濃度反應曲線比較 AMM/RMM 與 CMM 之準確度可比性

原文內容 Original Text

The analyses of accuracy in Section 10.1 treated the spiked concentration levels as a categorical variable, while the spiked concentration levels were treated as a continuous variable for the linearity assessment in Section 10.2.1 and Section 10.2.2. The two analyses on accuracy and linearity together can then be used to make a statement about the accuracy for concentration levels other than those tested in the experiment. An alternative approach is to model accuracy as a function of the concentration level and to establish a 90% confidence interval at each concentration that can be compared with the non-inferiority margin. Section 10.2.3 discusses the data analysis approach that models the concentration-response curves for the AMM/RMM and CMM separately and then uses these curves to calculate the accuracy of the AMM/RMM with respect to the CMM.

Note: This type of data analysis is rather technical and may require the help of a statistician to be able to program it in a programmable statistical software package such as SAS®, R, or Python; the software TriMSA has already implemented such an analysis. To aid readers, Section 10.3.3 provides some formulae that could be implemented in their preferred software package using the data shown in Table 10.2.3-1.

The data from Table 10.2.3-1 will be used to illustrate this approach of calculating accuracy through concentration-response curves. It is assumed that the counts for both the AMM/RMM and CMM are either normally or otherwise Poisson-distributed. The counts have been visualized in Figure 10.2.3-1, where the mean counts per spiked concentration are connected. The figure shows that the concentration-response curve is nonlinear in spiked concentration.

Figure 10.2.3-1 Visualization of the Counts per Concentration and Connecting the Mean Counts

For both microbiological methods, the Mitscherlich function is appropriate to use to extend the concentration-response curves to nonlinear relationships in spiked concentrations:

m(λ) ≡ E(y|λ)  =  β1 + β2·exp{β3·log(λ)}

Where: E(y|λ) = expected concentration; λ = concentration level; β1 = intercept; β2 = slope; β3 = power parameter.

The Mitscherlich function is a so-called nonlinear regression model and requires specific regression analysis tools to estimate this function. It is relatively flexible in modeling concentration-response curves and has broad applicability. When the intercept is zero (β1 = 0), the Mitscherlich function becomes log-linear:

log(E(y|λ))  =  log(β2) + β3·log(λ)

When the power parameter is equal to one (β3 = 1), the Mitscherlich function becomes a linear function in the concentration λ:

E(y|λ)  =  β1 + β2λ

Finally, when both the intercept is zero and the power parameter is equal to one, the relation between the mean count and concentration level becomes proportional. Thus, under certain conditions, the nonlinear Mitscherlich function becomes a (log-) linear function, and it can also take the shape of a proportional linear model.

When the counts are Poisson-distributed, a nonlinear Poisson regression analysis must be applied. Most general-purpose statistical software cannot manage the nonlinear aspect, and specialized software is required. The Mitscherlich function with Poisson-distributed counts can be run in SAS®, R, and TriMSA. If the counts are assumed to be normally distributed, the Mitscherlich function should be estimated with a weighted nonlinear regression analysis. The weights are needed to address the heteroscedasticity in the counts across concentrations (which is not needed with a Poisson regression analysis), and the nonlinearity is needed to fit the Mitscherlich function. Such regression analysis is available in SAS®, R, and Minitab. While the results of both regression analyses can be obtained, calculating the accuracy of the AMM/RMM against CMM is even more complicated with the weighted nonlinear regression analysis than with the nonlinear Poisson regression analysis, because a model for the variance of the counts across the spiked concentrations must be determined. In the Poisson analysis, this variance function is determined by the Poisson-distribution. This technical report illustrates the accuracy for the nonlinear Poisson regression analysis in Section 10.2.3.1 and the weighted nonlinear regression analysis in Section 10.2.3.2.

導師解析 Tutorial Commentary

核心概念解析 Key Concepts

Categorical vs. Continuous 濃度處理方式: Section 10.1 把每個 spiked concentration 當作獨立的「類別」分別檢定準確度（例如 5 CFU、25 CFU 各自算一次回收率與信賴區間），完全不假設濃度之間有函數關係；Section 10.2.1／10.2.2 則把濃度當作「連續變數」，用一條迴歸曲線同時描述所有濃度。10.2.3 更進一步：直接用「曲線本身」來計算 AMM/RMM 對 CMM 的非劣性，而不是先分別做線性檢定再做逐點準確度檢定兩件事。

Mitscherlich Function（米契利希函數): 一個彈性極高的非線性函數 m(λ)=β1+β2·λ^β3，透過三個參數（截距 β1、斜率 β2、冪次 β3）可以涵蓋從「比例關係」到「飽和曲線」的各種濃度反應型態，是農業科學中歷史悠久（作物產量對施肥量的反應曲線）、被本文借用到微生物計數建模的經典非線性模型。

比喻說明 Analogy

Mitscherlich 函數就像一台「可調式」的萬用曲線產生器：轉動 β3（冪次）這個旋鈕，曲線可以從一直線（β3=1）調整成往上彎（β3>1，訊號加速成長）或往下彎（β3<1，訊號逐漸飽和）；再把 β1（截距）歸零，曲線就會強制通過原點。這種「一個模型、多種形狀」的設計，讓分析人員不需要一開始就猜對曲線形狀，而是讓資料本身「投票」決定最終形狀為何。

重點提示 Key Notes

本節強調兩種配適 Mitscherlich 函數的路徑各有優劣：非線性 Poisson 迴歸（10.2.3.1）的變異數結構由 Poisson 分布本身決定（均值=變異數），不需要另外建模；加權非線性迴歸（10.2.3.2）則需要額外對「變異數如何隨濃度變化」建立模型，計算過程更複雜。原文也坦承此類分析屬於「相當技術性」的統計工作，實務上多半需要統計師協助，並提及專用軟體 TriMSA 已內建此類分析——這對評估外部方法驗證報告是否具備足夠統計嚴謹度，是一個重要的查核點。

公式與計算 Formula

Mitscherlich 函數（一般型）：
m(λ) ≡ E(y|λ) = β1 + β2·exp{β3·log(λ)} = β1 + β2·λ^β3

β1 = 0            →  Log-linear: log(E(y|λ)) = log(β2) + β3·log(λ)
β3 = 1            →  Linear:     E(y|λ) = β1 + β2·λ
β1 = 0 且 β3 = 1  →  Proportional（比例關係）

β1 = 截距（濃度為 0 時的期望計數）
β2 = 斜率（尺度參數）
β3 = 冪次參數（曲線彎曲方向與程度）

圖表解讀 Figure Analysis

Figure 10.2.3-1 使用 Table 10.2.3-1 的新範例資料（與 Table 10.1-1 不同的另一組實驗數據），將各濃度的平均計數以直線連接。可觀察到連接線並非一條完美直線，尤其在低濃度區段的曲度較明顯，這正是原文所說「濃度反應曲線在 spiked concentration 上呈非線性」的視覺證據，也是後續必須引入 Mitscherlich 函數（而非簡單線性迴歸）的原因。

10.2.3.1 Using Nonlinear Poisson Regression Analysis 使用非線性 Poisson 迴歸分析

原文內容 Original Text

Fitting the Mitscherlich function to the data in Table 10.2.3-1 for both microbiological methods separately, results in the estimates of the parameters of the Mitscherlich function and its 95% confidence intervals shown in Table 10.2.3.1-1.

The fitted Mitscherlich functions have been plotted to the observed counts in Figure 10.2.3.1-1.

Figure 10.2.3.1-1 Visualization of the Estimated Mitscherlich Functions with Respect to the Observed Counts

The two microbiological methods show a different concentration-response curve. The CMM has some difficulty enumerating microorganisms at lower concentrations but improves when the concentration increases. This can be seen from a slope less than one and a power parameter larger than one. The AMM/RMM shows an opposite pattern, where enumeration is good at lower concentrations but worsens when concentrations increase. This pattern reflects a slope larger than one and a power parameter smaller than one.

Both power parameter estimates deviate from one significantly (the value one does not fall in the 95% confidence interval), but the intercepts may be equal to zero, which may suggest a log-linear model. This model can be fitted with the same procedure, by setting the intercept to zero and locking this as the value so that it will no longer be estimated and, therefore, remains equal to zero. The estimated parameters for the log-linear model are shown in Table 10.2.3.1-2.

By comparing Akaike's corrected information criterion for the log-linear and the Mitscherlich function for both microbiological methods separately, the log-linear model appears to be a better fit (AMM/RMM: Mitscherlich 224.8 versus log-linear 222.4; CMM: Mitscherlich 208.9 versus log-linear 206.8). Thus, using the log-linear concentration-response curves can be continued.

To determine non-inferiority in enumeration between the AMM/RMM and CMM, the recovery or ratio of the two estimated concentration-response curves can be calculated for each concentration in the experimental range [5, 250]: m̂A(λ)/m̂C(λ). For this ratio, a lower 95% confidence limit can be calculated and then compared to the lower limit with the non-inferiority margin.

The lower 95% confidence limit is best calculated in the logarithmic scale:

[m̂A(λ) / m̂C(λ)] · exp{ −1.645·√(τ̂A²(λ) + τ̂C²(λ)) }

with τA²(λ) = VAR(log(m̂A(λ))) and τC²(λ) = VAR(log(m̂C(λ))) the variance of the estimated log transformed Mitscherlich function of the AMM/RMM and CMM, respectively.

The variance of the estimated logarithmically transformed Mitscherlich function is quite elaborative and can be found in Heidari et al. (2022) (16). For the log-linear model, the variance τ²(λ) is somewhat less elaborate and is equal to:

τ²(λ)  =  VAR(log(β̂2)) + [log(λ)]²·VAR(β̂3) + 2·log(λ)·COV(log(β̂2), β̂3)

To obtain this variance, it is easier to model the slope parameter in the log scale (as is provided in TriMSA).

The estimated recovery (solid line) and the lower 95% confidence limit (dotted line) is shown in Figure 10.2.3.1-2 (left figure). The procedure NLMIXED in SAS® for the analysis and the visualization was used for Figure 10.2.3.1-2, but TriMSA can provide the same results. The data show that the AMM/RMM is non-inferior to the CMM (at non-inferiority margin of 70%), but the recovery of the AMM/RMM is much better at the lower end of the concentration range than at the upper range. This is due to the enumeration pattern seen from the two microbiological methods separately. Finally, the lower 95% confidence limit at 250 CFU is estimated at 82.7%, so non-inferiority would not have been rejected at 80% non-inferiority margin either.

Figure 10.2.3.1-2 Visualization of the Estimated Recovery for the Log-Linear Concentration Response Curves of the Microbiological Methods

This model-based analysis for accuracy could sometimes help reduce variation compared to a per concentration analysis and, therefore, can be more efficient than the analyses between the AMM/RMM and CMM with concentration used as categorical variable. The data in Table 10.1-1 is used to illustrate this. The analysis in Section 10.1.2 with the results presented in Table 10.1.3-1 shows that non-inferiority between AMM/RMM and CMM occurs at 25 CFU for the first time. However, since proportionality for both the AMM/RMM and CMM on the concentration-response curves was demonstrated, consistent accuracy across the full range of 5 to 250 CFU was also demonstrated. Therefore, non-inferiority could be extended across the full experimental range. But if proportionality did not hold for at least one of the microbiological methods, non-inferiority below 25 CFU could not be claimed (see Table 10.1.3-1). If the log-linear models were the appropriate models for the concentration-response curves and the model-based approach for accuracy is applied, it would show that non-inferiority would begin from 8.4 CFU (see Figure 10.2.3.1-2), which is below the 25 CFU.

導師解析 Tutorial Commentary

核心概念解析 Key Concepts

AICC（Akaike's corrected Information Criterion）: 用來在「配適度」與「模型複雜度」之間權衡的指標，數值越小代表模型越適合。本例中 log-linear（鎖定截距=0，只用 2 個參數 β2、β3）反而比完整 Mitscherlich（3 個參數）AICC 更低（AMM/RMM: 222.4 vs 224.8；CMM: 206.8 vs 208.9），代表「更簡單的模型」在此資料上表現更好——這呼應了統計學的簡約原則（parsimony）：不要為了配適資料而過度複雜化模型。

Ratio-of-Curves Non-inferiority（曲線比值非劣性法）: 不再逐濃度分別檢定，而是直接計算兩條配適曲線在「任一濃度 λ」下的比值 m̂A(λ)/m̂C(λ) 作為回收率估計，並在對數尺度上計算其信賴下限——這讓非劣性結論可以連續地涵蓋整個實驗濃度區間 [5, 250]，而不只是幾個離散的測試點。

比喻說明 Analogy

把「逐濃度類別比較」想像成只在路上設 6 個測速照相點，車速在這 6 點合法，但中間路段完全沒有監控；「曲線比值法」則像是全程雷達測速，畫出一條連續的速度曲線並直接證明整條路都沒超速。後者需要更精細的建模工具（雷達技術／非線性迴歸），但換來的是對「全程」而非「六個點」的保證——這正是為何本例能把非劣性下限從 25 CFU 一路延伸到 8.4 CFU。

重點提示 Key Notes

本節結尾特別點出模型比較法的商業價值：在 Section 10.1.2／10.1.3（逐濃度類別比較）中，AMM/RMM 對 CMM 的非劣性最低只能證明到 25 CFU；但若能證明兩方法的濃度反應曲線都符合 log-linear（或更嚴格的比例性），用「以模型為本」的方法可以把非劣性下限延伸到 8.4 CFU——足足降低了近 3 倍的可宣稱下限濃度。但原文也提醒但書：如果任一方法的比例性不成立，就不能把非劣性延伸到 25 CFU 以下，代表這個效益完全仰賴線性/比例性假設是否成立，不能想當然爾套用。

公式與計算 Formula

回收率之對數尺度信賴下限（Lower 95% CL）：

[ m̂A(λ) / m̂C(λ) ] · exp{ −1.645·√(τ̂A²(λ) + τ̂C²(λ)) }

m̂A(λ), m̂C(λ) = AMM/RMM、CMM 配適曲線在濃度 λ 的期望值
τA²(λ), τC²(λ) = log(m̂A(λ))、log(m̂C(λ)) 的變異數

Log-linear 模型的變異數（較簡化版本）：
τ²(λ) = VAR(log(β̂2)) + [log(λ)]²·VAR(β̂3)
        + 2·log(λ)·COV(log(β̂2), β̂3)

結果：250 CFU 處回收率信賴下限 = 82.7%
      → 即使非劣性 margin 提高到 80%，結論依然不變

圖表解讀 Figure Analysis

Figure 10.2.3.1-1 顯示 Mitscherlich 函數配適曲線與觀察計數的關係：CMM（左圖）曲線在低濃度處略微上凸（低濃度偵測不足、隨濃度增加逐漸追上），AMM/RMM（右圖）則相反，低濃度時已相對貼近實際、高濃度處出現輕微飽和（曲線略低於資料點延伸趨勢）——這與斜率、冪次參數的估計結果（Table 10.2.3.1-1）完全吻合。

Figure 10.2.3.1-2 是本節的核心產出：左圖為 CMM 估計回收率（實線）與 95% 信賴下限（虛線），右圖為 AMM/RMM。可觀察到 AMM/RMM 的回收率曲線在低濃度時甚至超過 100%，隨濃度增加而略降，但信賴下限全程維持在 70% 非劣性門檻之上（甚至在 250 CFU 處達 82.7%，滿足 80% 更嚴格的門檻）——這正是「以模型為本」分析法能提供連續、全區間非劣性宣稱的視覺證據。

實務應用 Practical Application

對於欲擴大放行測試靈敏度下限（例如把 AMM/RMM 的可宣稱下限從 25 CFU 降到接近 LoD/LoQ 附近）的 CDMO 專案，若能在方法驗證階段額外執行非線性 Poisson 迴歸並證明 log-linear 曲線成立，即可用同一批實驗數據「免費」把非劣性宣稱範圍向下延伸，而不需要再多做低濃度的驗證批次——這是顯著節省驗證成本與時程的統計策略，但必須配合統計師執行嚴謹的模型選擇（AICC）與診斷（見 Section 10.1.1.3 的 lack-of-fit 概念延伸）。

練習思考 Practice Questions

  1. 為什麼本例最終選擇「鎖定截距=0 的 log-linear 模型」而非完整的三參數 Mitscherlich 函數？判斷依據是什麼統計指標？
  2. 若某一濃度反應曲線的比例性（proportionality）無法被證明成立，「以模型為本」的非劣性延伸法還能否套用到 25 CFU 以下的濃度？

10.2.3.2 Using Weighted Nonlinear Regression Analysis 使用加權非線性迴歸分析

原文內容 Original Text

Using the data in Table 10.2.3-1 for both microbiological methods separately and using weighted nonlinear regression the estimated results of the parameters of the Mitscherlich function and its 95% confidence intervals are shown in Table 10.2.3.2-1.

Here, the weights have been selected equal to one over the variance of the counts for each spiked concentration, the same as was done for weighted linear regression in Section 10.2.1. Figure 10.2.3-4 provides a visualization of the data and the fitted Mitscherlich function.

Figure 10.2.3-4 Visualization of the Estimated Mitscherlich Functions Using Weighted Non-Linear Regression with Respect to the Observed Counts

The coefficients are rather different from the coefficients estimated by the nonlinear Poisson regression, particularly for the intercept and slope, but the conclusion about the enumeration patterns do not change. The CMM still has more enumeration issues at lower concentration levels, while the AMM/RMM has more enumeration issues at higher concentration levels. Also, the conclusions that the intercept may be equal to zero and that the power parameters deviate from one are the same as with the nonlinear Poisson regression analysis.

Furthermore, the predicted curves are not so different from the nonlinear Poisson regression analysis in Figure 10.2.3-2, even though the coefficients of the Mitscherlich function are somewhat different. However, visually, the nonlinear Poisson regression analysis seems to fit slightly better than the weighted nonlinear regression analysis and, therefore, may be preferred over the weighted nonlinear regression.

導師解析 Tutorial Commentary

核心概念解析 Key Concepts

加權非線性迴歸（Weighted Nonlinear Regression）: 與 10.2.1 節的加權線性迴歸邏輯一致——以「各濃度計數變異數的倒數」作為權重，但這裡配適的是非線性 Mitscherlich 函數而非直線。與 10.2.3.1 節的非線性 Poisson 迴歸相比，兩者都能配適同一個 Mitscherlich 函數形式，但變異數結構的來源不同：Poisson 迴歸的變異數由分布假設「內建」決定，加權非線性迴歸則需要分析人員「外部」提供一組權重（本例沿用各濃度樣本變異數的倒數）。

比喻說明 Analogy

可以把非線性 Poisson 迴歸與加權非線性迴歸想像成兩位廚師用同一份食譜（Mitscherlich 函數）做同一道菜，但一位遵循「食譜內建比例」（Poisson 分布自動決定變異數結構），另一位則「自行秤重調整」各項食材比例（外部指定權重）。兩人做出來的菜（配適曲線）外觀相似、口味結論一致（CMM 低濃度弱、AMM/RMM 高濃度弱），但精確的調味比例（係數估計值）略有不同。

重點提示 Key Notes

本節的結論具有重要的「穩健性驗證」意義：即使改用完全不同的統計方法（加權非線性迴歸 vs. 非線性 Poisson 迴歸），關於兩方法「濃度反應型態」的科學結論（CMM 低濃度弱、AMM/RMM 高濃度弱，截距≈0，冪次≠1）完全一致。這種「用不同方法得到相同結論」的交叉驗證，是提升方法驗證報告可信度的重要證據；原文最終仍建議優先採用非線性 Poisson 迴歸，因其配適度在視覺上略優，且變異數結構有分布理論支持，不需額外假設權重來源。

公式與計算 Formula

加權非線性迴歸權重設定（與 10.2.1 節加權線性迴歸相同邏輯）：

權重 wᵢ = 1 / Var(y | λᵢ)
        （各 spiked concentration 之計數樣本變異數的倒數）

配適目標：Mitscherlich 函數
m(λ) = β1 + β2·λ^β3
在加權平方和準則下求解 β1, β2, β3

圖表解讀 Figure Analysis

Figure 10.2.3-4 呈現加權非線性迴歸配適的 Mitscherlich 曲線（CMM 左圖、AMM/RMM 右圖），與 Figure 10.2.3.1-1（非線性 Poisson 迴歸）視覺上高度相似——曲線走勢、資料點分布幾乎一致，僅在細節配適上略有差異。這正是原文所說「預測曲線相去不遠，但視覺上非線性 Poisson 迴歸配適略佳」的圖像證據，讀者可將兩圖並排比較以驗證此一結論。

實務應用 Practical Application

當內部或客戶的統計軟體平台不支援非線性 Poisson 迴歸（例如僅有 Minitab 而無 SAS®/R 授權)，加權非線性迴歸提供了一條可行的替代路徑，讓 CDMO 仍能在既有軟體工具下配適 Mitscherlich 函數並得到方向一致的科學結論。但應在方法驗證報告中明確記載「本分析未採用 Poisson 分布假設之變異數結構，而是採用外部估計權重」，以利未來稽核追溯分析選擇的合理性。

練習思考 Practice Questions

  1. 加權非線性迴歸與非線性 Poisson 迴歸兩者對「變異數結構」的處理方式有何本質差異？
  2. 若兩種迴歸方法得到的科學結論一致但係數估計值不同，這對方法驗證報告的可信度分別代表什麼意義？

本節重點回顧 Section Summary

  • 線性驗證在微生物學方法中的意義，是把 Section 10.1 少數濃度點上證明的準確度，透過單調（monotonic）或線性/log-linear 的濃度反應曲線，安全延伸到未測試的濃度範圍——這與分析化學儀器單點校正所要求的「線性」意義並不相同。
  • 加權線性迴歸（10.2.1）用截距、R²、二次項檢定判斷線性與比例性；Poisson 迴歸（10.2.2）則用對數連結函數的斜率判斷比例性與飽和效應，兩者殊途同歸但假設與檢定邏輯不同，實務上建議搭配 lack-of-fit 分析交叉驗證。
  • Mitscherlich 函數（β1+β2·λ^β3）提供了涵蓋比例、線性、log-linear、飽和曲線的統一非線性框架；透過 AICC 比較可判斷是否能簡化為 log-linear 模型，並用非線性 Poisson 迴歸或加權非線性迴歸兩種途徑配適。
  • 「以模型為本」的濃度反應曲線比值法（m̂A(λ)/m̂C(λ)）能在整個實驗濃度區間連續建立非劣性信賴下限，相較逐濃度類別比較法能大幅延伸可宣稱的非劣性濃度下限（本例從 25 CFU 延伸至 8.4 CFU），但此效益完全仰賴比例性/線性假設成立，需審慎以統計檢定驗證後才能宣稱。
